title: Practice with a partner
hook: a shared ritual with someone you love: Tobias asked Sarah to rise and pray with him, and she said the amen too
tomorrow: what did Jesus do when his friends shooed the kids away?

segments.voice: Last line of the body stretch: this body. Sleep, food, breath, rest and care, all on one page. Now the rule turns outward, to the people in it.

Sunday pancakes, the walk after dinner, the same song in the car: a couple's one thing that's theirs. The book of Tobit has a couple whose first night needed more than a song. Sarah had been married seven times, and each time, on the wedding night, a demon named Asmodeus killed the husband. Now Tobias has married her, guided by a traveling companion who is secretly the angel Raphael. The door shuts. Before morning, her father will be outside, digging a grave.
screen: `ONE THING THAT'S THEIRS.` → `SEVEN WEDDING NIGHTS.` → `THE DOOR SHUTS.` → `BEFORE MORNING, A GRAVE.`

segments.voice: Tobias does what Raphael told him. He lays the heart and liver of a fish on the coals of the incense, and the smoke drives the demon off. Then, before anything else, he gets up and says: "Sister, arise, and let us pray that God would have pity on us." He doesn't pray over her while she watches. He asks her to rise with him. His prayer remembers Adam, and Eve given to him as a helper and a stay, and asks "that we may become aged together." And then the line that makes it shared: "And she said with him, Amen." Two voices, one amen. In the morning, the grave gets filled back in. So what does the story teach? Tobit is a Jewish story, kept in the Bibles of Catholic and Orthodox Christians; the Jewish Bible doesn't include it, and Protestant Bibles that print it set it among the Apocrypha. Catholic wedding readings include this very prayer. In the story, a marriage starts with two people standing up together and asking for the same thing, out loud. Not one partner's practice with the other one watching. For two people now, it can be very small: one line before dinner, a candle, a walk where each of you names one good thing. What makes it practice with a partner is the amen. Both of you say yes.
screen: `SMOKE DRIVES THE DEMON OFF.` · `SISTER, ARISE, AND LET US PRAY.` · `AND SHE SAID WITH HIM, AMEN.` · `A MARRIAGE BEGUN WITH A SHARED PRAYER.` · then, large: `TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Write one small thing you could share with someone you love: a line, a walk, a candle, a meal. Keep it short enough for two people to say yes to. Then sit tall, the way Tobias stood up first, and let the breath come and go.
Practice with a partner: a small ritual two people share, both saying yes to it, like Tobias and Sarah's one amen.
Your line: together. Two voices, and one amen at the end. Day 1653, and a new stretch begins: others.

screen: `DAY 1653 COUNTS.` → `OTHERS · 1 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DID JESUS DO WHEN HIS FRIENDS SHOOED THE KIDS AWAY?`

howItsDone: Couples on many paths keep small shared rituals: a blessing before a meal, candles on Friday night, a prayer or a thank-you said together at bedtime. Tobias and Sarah's prayer from Tobit 8 is among the readings offered for Catholic weddings.
